prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1369; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the policyholder reported a low-speed collision in a shopping center parking lot, with the claimant stating she was the front passenger in the other vehicle involved. Initial contact made and the claimant's representing attorney has asked that all communication be directed to their office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the first notice of loss and the photos submitted by the policyholder, which confirm the general location and the positions of both vehicles after impact. Police report on file notes the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene.

Entry 3: Spoke with the driver, who lives with the policyholder and is listed as a household member on the policy, and confirmed coverage applies to this operator. Driver described the impact in the same way as in the initial report.

Entry 4: Inspected the damaged vehicle with the repair estimate. The damage is largely consistent with the impact described, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the owner's account.

Entry 5: Checked coverage history and found nothing suggesting the damage predates the policy inception, so the loss falls within the current term.

Entry 6: Attorney submitted the claimant's medical records, which document a neck strain. The diagnosed injury fits the kind and force of a collision of this type.

Entry 7: Reviewed the treatment timeline. Care followed a usual course, with visits tapering as the claimant's symptoms improved. Records also mention a small strain in the same area several years ago that healed fully.

Entry 8: Took a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. Account matched the account given in each prior conversation, with no changes to the sequence of events.

Entry 9: Asked for independent witness contact information. None was provided, and the photos are the only independent confirmation of details beyond the police report and the parties' statements.

Entry 10: Evaluation is ongoing. Injury, treatment, and property damage are being assessed together, and a summary will go to the supervisor once the remaining medical bills arrive.
